editorial:
Imagine starting your first year of college all excited, only to have one bad night ruin everything. You meet Selena, a shy freshman who just wants to do her work, but her roommate Amy pushes her into a wild party scene. Things go south fast when Selena is attacked, leaving her with a physical and emotional scar that changes her whole life. You really feel for her as she tries to survive the school year while dealing with a heavy burden and a lot of pain. It is a heavy start, but the movie shifts into a story about trying to find happiness again through a kind teacher's assistant and a supportive professor.

What really hits home is how the movie handles the tension when Selena's attacker comes back into the picture. The acting feels real, though the pacing slows down a bit in the middle. If you enjoy dramas that mix romance with a bit of a mystery, you will like this one. Since it is an older indie film, your best bet is hunting for a digital rental on Apple TV or checking if it is streaming in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to get the best picture quality. It is definitely a movie that makes you think about trust and healing.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head when the man who attacked Selena returns to mess with her life. You find out that the romance she thought was saving her had some secrets attached to it. In the end, Selena has to face her fear and the person who hurt her to finally move on. She finds the strength to stop being a victim and takes control of her future, leaving the trauma behind for a fresh start.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about survival and overcoming hard times.
